prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by designed small molecules that bring a chosen protein to an E3 ubiquitin ligase

statement.case_for: After the first round I keep targeted protein degradation as my single preferred part, and I have narrowed what I am prepared to defend. The achievement is the design principle: a small molecule that induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a chosen target, so that the cell destroys the protein instead of the drug occupying a site. It is new, it is quantitative (ternary-complex cooperativity, linker and ligand optimisation, structure-guided VHL recruiters), it is confirmed in many independent laboratories, and it has already changed what chemists try to make. That meets my game-changer test. It is also the only shortlisted candidacy that the whole committee treats as scientifically serious, and the chair's summary shows four explicit supporters against three for base editing and two for C-N coupling. I do not treat the count as a substitute for judgment, but it matters that no one disputes the chemistry; the disagreement is about timing and names. On names, Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated the PROTAC concept in 2001, and Ciulli turned it into a design discipline with the VHL ligands and the structural account of the ternary complex. A citation written around designed induced proximity describes exactly what those three did and does not claim the cereblon glue discovery.
statement.case_against: My two reservations from round 1 are unchanged and I will not hide them. First, maturity: to my knowledge no degrader is yet an approved drug, so a prize now rests on mechanism and trial activity more than on delivered benefit. Second, attribution: the cereblon strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) explains how thalidomide analogues work and has the stronger clinical footprint, and a three-name PROTAC prize leaves it unrecognised. If the committee concludes the glue mechanism is inseparable from this prize, my trio is not defensible and I would rather wait a few years than split credit badly. Chabes's Handa-for-Ciulli swap is the most serious form of this objection. My reasoning against it is that Ciulli's structural and design contribution belongs to the PROTAC line that the citation names, whereas Handa's discovery is a different achievement that deserves its own recognition later and does not fit as a third name here.

responses.point: Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli for base editing as the sole prize, arguing that cytosine and adenine editors are separate chemical achievements and that the absence of a double-strand break makes the reaction different from Cas9 cleavage.
responses.response: I accept that deamination of a displaced strand without a cut is a different reaction from Cas9 cleavage, and that the evolution of TadA to act on DNA is non-obvious. That narrows my novelty objection but does not remove it, because the platform that positions the deaminase is the one recognised in 2020, and the field is about ten years old with a short clinical record and off-target and bystander data still accumulating. Your trio is also the configuration that most clearly leaves Kondo and Nishida outside the prize, which you yourself call a real gap. On the attribution questions I put to you, my view is that Komor and Gaudelli are credibly the lead experimentalists, so I no longer argue for Liu alone as cleanest. I still rank base editing below degradation on maturity and on distance from an earlier prize, and I would not vote against it as an alternative.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, pairs base editing for Liu alone with degradation for Crews and Deshaies only, as two explainable chemical-biology stories within three people.
responses.response: I follow the logic of keeping the union at three, but I do not think the pairing helps either part. Dropping Ciulli leaves out the structure-guided VHL work and the ternary-complex rules that made PROTACs a design discipline and not an idea, and a Liu-only part invites the Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida dispute you list yourself. A prize that stacks two contested attributions is harder to defend than one prize with a coherent trio. I would rather the committee first decide which single candidacy can reach five votes, which is what you asked in your summary. I would, however, accept your question of whether a limited citation helps: yes, a citation limited to the designed-degrader mechanism makes my maturity worry smaller, though not zero.

responses.point: Somfai pairs C-N coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) with Liu alone for base editing, and says B008 should stand alone as a two-laureate prize if B061 is not accepted.
responses.response: I agree that Buchwald and Hartwig are as clean an attribution as the list offers and that Kosugi was a precursor, not a co-laureate. Your point that the 2010 prize did not cover amination is correct, and Zou's argument that C-N reductive elimination needed a different ligand solution is persuasive to me. My remaining difficulty is conceptual novelty: palladium-catalysed bond formation was already honoured, so I weigh B008 as a strong and safe candidate with less of a game-changer character than degradation. Answering the chair's question, I would support B008 as a stand-alone two-person prize if the committee cannot reach five on degradation, and I have put it among my alternatives for that reason.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved to B028 only after the opening record, but says the cereblon glue discovery is arguably the more decisive chemical insight and that expert reports should settle the attribution.
responses.response: I agree that the glue strand is the hardest point for a PROTAC trio, and I share your caution on maturity. Where I differ is on whether the glue discovery must be in the same prize: cereblon explained a known drug, whereas the PROTAC line created something chemists can design on purpose, and a citation that says so does not need to carry the glue strand. If the expert reports show that the two cannot be separated in the literature, I would withdraw my preference. You also raise whether ab initio dynamics is chemistry in the statutory sense; given that my own B037 is a computational candidacy with no other first place, I accept that I cannot carry it as my configuration and keep it only as an alternative.

responses.point: Aili argues that the criterion is a discovery of great benefit and not an approved-drug count, and that mechanism confirmation and human proof of concept make recognition timely.
responses.response: That is a fair statement of the criterion, and I accept that approval is not the test. My point is narrower: benefit has to be visible, not only expected, and trials with human proof of concept are the evidence for that. I am willing to support the prize now if the citation is limited to the design principle and the mechanism, which is the answer to the chair's question. On the third name I would keep Ciulli and not Handa for the reasons given above, and I agree with you that the glue strand should be kept apart from this part.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that mechanism confirmation and trial evidence are enough for a degrader prize in the absence of an approved PROTAC drug.
Whether the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) can be separated from PROTACs in a citation, or whether the expert reports will show it is inseparable.
Whether Ciulli rather than Handa should hold the third place, and what criterion the committee uses between a design contribution and a mechanism discovery.
Whether the committee will see B061 as too close to the 2020 prize, and whether B008 could stand alone as a safe fallback if no candidacy reaches five votes.
statement.conflict_note: No change. My postdoc with Arieh Warshel and my work on simulation of enzymes and ligand binding make me close to the computational candidacies B037 and B001, but I have no direct collaboration with any named candidate and do not think recusal is needed. B037 appears only as an alternative, and none of my preferred names is a collaborator or Uppsala colleague.
